about: The hymn begins with the song of the angels at the birth of Christ. It praises God the Father and then addresses Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son and Lamb of God, asking Him to have mercy on us and receive our prayer. It ends by professing the glory of Christ with the Holy Spirit in the glory of God the Father.

s01.narrative: At the middle of the altar, the priest extends and joins his hands, bows his head slightly and, if the hymn is to be said, begins it with “Glória in excélsis Deo”. The priest continues with hands joined.

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae rubric before Gloria in excelsis

s02.translation: Glory to God in the highest.

s03.translation: And on earth peace to people of good will.

s04.translation: We praise You. We bless You. We adore You. We glorify You.

s05.translation: We give You thanks for Your great glory.

s06.translation: Lord God, heavenly King, O God, almighty Father.

s08.translation: Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father.

s09.translation: You take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

s10.translation: You take away the sins of the world, receive our prayer.

s11.translation: You are seated at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us.

s12.translation: For You alone are the Holy One. You alone are the Lord. You alone are the Most High, Jesus Christ.

s13.translation: With the Holy Spirit in the glory of God the Father. Amen.

w001.function: A nominal sentence with “let there be” understood. “Deo” (w004) identifies the recipient of the glory.

w003.function: A neuter adjective used substantively: “in the highest [places]”.

w011.function: With “bonæ” (w010), it forms a genitive of quality modifying “homínibus” (w009).

w021.function: With “Grátias” (w020), it forms the fixed expression “grátias ágere” — to give thanks.

w028.function: “Deus” has the same form in the nominative and vocative. Here it is vocative, parallel to “Dómine” (w027).

w041.function: Nominative used as an address in the series following “Dómine” (w039) and “Deus” (w040).

w043.function: Nominative used as an address, parallel to “Agnus” (w041).

w045.function: Subject of “tollis” (w046). The second person follows from the direct address to Christ.

w061.function: “ad” (w060) with the accusative marks position here: at the right hand of the Father.

w067.function: With “tu” (w066) it forms a sentence without an expressed verb: “Thou alone [art] holy”. The next two occurrences of solus have the same construction.
